import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from datetime import datetime

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
colors = sns.color_palette("husl", 8)

# 1. Sales by Product
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
product_sales = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
ax1.bar(product_sales.index, product_sales.values, color=colors[0])
ax1.set_title('Total Sales by Product', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Product')
ax1.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Sales by Time of Day
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
df['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(df['time'], format='%H:%M').dt.hour
hourly_sales = df.groupby('hour')['total'].sum()
ax2.plot(hourly_sales.index, hourly_sales.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, color=colors[1])
ax2.set_title('Sales by Hour of Day', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Hour')
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 3. Payment Method Distribution
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
payment_counts = df['payment_method'].value_counts()
ax3.pie(payment_counts.values, labels=payment_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=[colors[2], colors[3]], startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Payment Method Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Sales by Age Group
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
age_sales = df.groupby('customer_age_group')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
ax4.barh(age_sales.index, age_sales.values, color=colors[4])
ax4.set_title('Total Sales by Age Group', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax4.set_ylabel('Age Group')

# 5. Product Size Distribution
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
size_counts = df['size'].value_counts()
ax5.bar(size_counts.index, size_counts.values, color=colors[5])
ax5.set_title('Orders by Size', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Size')
ax5.set_ylabel('Number of Orders')

# 6. Takeaway vs Dine-in
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
takeaway_sales = df.groupby('is_takeaway')['total'].sum()
labels = ['Dine-in', 'Takeaway']
ax6.pie(takeaway_sales.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=[colors[6], colors[7]], startangle=90)
ax6.set_title('Takeaway vs Dine-in Sales', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 7. Average Price by Product
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
avg_price = df.groupby('product')['price'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
ax7.bar(avg_price.index, avg_price.values, color=colors[0], alpha=0.7)
ax7.set_title('Average Price by Product', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Product')
ax7.set_ylabel('Average Price ($)')
ax7.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 8. Quantity Distribution
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
ax8.hist(df['quantity'], bins=range(1, df['quantity'].max()+2), 
         color=colors[1], alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
ax8.set_title('Quantity Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Quantity per Order')
ax8.set_ylabel('Frequency')

# 9. Summary Statistics
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.axis('off')
summary_text = f"""
Summary Statistics:

Total Orders: {len(df)}
Total Revenue: ${df['total'].sum():.2f}
Average Order Value: ${df['total'].mean():.2f}

Most Popular Product:
{product_sales.index[0]}

Peak Hour: {hourly_sales.idxmax()}:00
"""
ax9.text(0.1, 0.5, summary_text, fontsize=11, verticalalignment='center',
         bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.3))

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
